resolutions.review_rationale: The existing metric open-ball definition is precisely B_d(a,r)={x:d(x,a)<r} for metric d and radius r>0. The metric-space topology source invokes the same object B_d(x,r), with its balls generating τ_d. Both contexts and full source statements match, and no normed-vector-space restriction is imposed.

The field-theoretic perfect closure k^perf named in the geometric-normality source is the smallest perfect extension of positive-characteristic k formed by adjoining all compatible p-power roots, precisely the existing perfect-closure meaning. Characteristic-zero convention is trivial (k^perf=k), no new meaning is required.

The common codomain (S,Σ_S) of independent random variables is exactly the existing definition of a measurable space: a set S equipped with its sigma-algebra Σ_S, and no probability measure on S is assumed. Random-variable independence remains source-specific.

A bounded linear transformation T:X→Y of normed vector spaces over a common scalar field ℝ or ℂ is first an ordinary F-linear transformation between vector spaces over one field, precisely the existing linear-transformation meaning. A global norm inequality and norm topology are separate boundedness conditions in the parent source.
